extracted.intended_audience: shippers, carriers, vessel owners/operators, governments, nongovernmental organizations, maritime standards bodies (e.g., IMO, ITF), and other stakeholders in international maritime shipping
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Maritime Commission Federal Register notice soliciting public comments and evidence on foreign vessel flagging laws, regulations, and practices (including flags of convenience, shadow fleets, and related owner/operator practices) and how those practices affect the efficiency, reliability, and safety of U.S. foreign trade ocean shipping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadline and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments on or before August 20, 2025. Comments must be written and in English, identified by Docket No. FMC-2025-0009, and submitted electronically via www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the instructions on Regulations.gov by searching for Docket No. FMC-2025-0009 and use the 'Submit a Comment' link. Contact David Eng (Secretary) for questions about submitting comments or confidential treatment (Phone: (202) 523-5725; Email: Secretary@fmc.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and confidential treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments shall be public under 46 CFR 502.291 unless confidential treatment is specifically requested for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If confidential treatment is desired, request it for good cause and follow the Commission's instructions; see contact information for questions. The Commission may withhold responses under 46 CFR 502.291 where authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requested content: evidence, experience, and data
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should contain evidence, experiences, and/or data relevant to the wide range of flagging practices across foreign nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete examples, empirical data, case studies, or firsthand experiences to support assertions about how flagging laws/practices affect shipping efficiency, safety, or reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific examples of responsible flagging laws, regulations, practices, and proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific examples of responsible flagging laws, regulations, practices, and proposals, including how they contribute or would contribute to the efficiency and reliability of the ocean shipping supply chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe which laws/practices, and explain mechanisms by which they improve efficiency, reliability, safety, environmental protection, crew welfare, transparency, inspections/certifications, and accountability (e.g., compliance with SOLAS, MARPOL, STCW).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific examples of unfavorable flagging laws, regulations, and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific examples of unfavorable flagging laws, regulations, and practices that endanger the efficiency and reliability of the ocean shipping supply chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete instances or patterns (e.g., lax oversight, minimal inspections, inadequate certification regimes) showing how these laws/practices lead to unsafe or unreliable shipping operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: How irresponsible flagging laws endanger efficiency and reliability (2.a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how irresponsible vessel flagging laws, regulations, and practices endanger the efficiency and reliability of the ocean shipping supply chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address mechanisms such as avoidance of inspections, poor maintenance, unsafe crewing, AIS/GPS spoofing or deactivation, and other operational failures that disrupt commerce and create risks to ports/infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of greatest-danger laws/practices (2.b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which irresponsible laws, regulations, and practices pose the greatest danger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rank or prioritize specific regulatory gaps or practices (e.g., open registries with no oversight, fraudulent registrations, lack of contactable registry offices) and explain the basis for that assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether irresponsible flagging fosters malign actors/fleets (2.c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address whether irresponsible vessel flagging laws, regulations, and practices foster the development of malign actors or fleets, such as the so-called shadow fleet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence or examples showing links between lax flagging regimes and illicit activities (sanctions evasion, smuggling, illegal fishing, human trafficking, organized crime).

rubrics_metrics.name: How irresponsible flagging endangers maritime infrastructure (2.d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how irresponsible vessel flagging laws, regulations, and practices endanger maritime infrastructure, such as ports, bridges, canals, and chokepoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include incident examples (e.g., vessel propulsion failures causing bridge strikes), risk analyses, and potential cascading effects on supply chains and critical infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practices by owners/operators undermining shipping efficiency — under/none insurance (3.a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe dangers posed by under-insured or uninsured vessels, including risks to other vessels, maritime infrastructure, and mariners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of incidents where inadequate insurance exacerbated harms or imposed costs on third parties or governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practices by owners/operators undermining shipping efficiency — poor maintenance (3.b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe dangers posed by vessels with poor or non-existent maintenance programs and few or no safety measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of maintenance-related failures (engine loss, fires, explosions) and explain how maintenance deficiencies correlate with flagging/registry practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practices by owners/operators undermining shipping efficiency — inexperienced ownership/management (3.c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe dangers posed by inexperienced vessel owners, operators, or agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how inexperienced management contributes to operational failures, regulatory evasion, or unsafe crewing and provide supporting examples or data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practices by owners/operators undermining shipping efficiency — unqualified mariners (3.d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe dangers posed by inexperienced or unqualified mariners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document examples where crew qualifications were inadequate, including failures to meet STCW standards, and resulting safety or operational incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practices by owners/operators undermining shipping efficiency — threats to freedom of navigation and AIS/GPS integrity (3.e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe dangers posed to freedom-of-navigation principles by irresponsible vessel owners and operators, such as dragging anchors damaging undersea cables/infrastructure, or through turning off, jamming, or spoofing AIS/GPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide incident reports, technical analyses, or trends (e.g., increased GPS jamming/spoofing distances) showing navigational interference and consequences for safety and commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of responsible vessel registration/flagging practices — potential benefits (4.a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe potential benefits to ocean shipping efficiency and reliability of standards for flagging laws, regulations, and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain expected outcomes such as reduced accidents, fewer disruptions, improved environmental compliance, better crew welfare, and increased transparency/accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most important responsible flagging laws/practices (4.b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the most important responsible flagging laws, regulations, and practices that contribute to the efficiency and reliability of ocean shipping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify particular laws, inspection regimes, certification requirements, registry oversight mechanisms, or enforcement tools and explain their contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: How Commission regulations could support responsible practices (4.c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how Commission regulations could support responsible flagging laws, regulations, and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer specific regulatory measures, enforcement approaches, information-sharing mechanisms, or incentives the FMC could adopt or recommend to promote compliance and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: How Commission regulations could deter irresponsible practices (4.d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how Commission regulations could deter irresponsible flagging laws, regulations, and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose deterrence mechanisms (e.g., market-based penalties, reporting/blacklisting, trade or administrative consequences) and provide rationale or evidence for effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs and burdens of deterring irresponsible flagging (5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the burdens to foreign nations and vessel operators or owners of irresponsible flagging practices (i.e., costs imposed by changes to deter such practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide assessments of economic, administrative, or operational burdens that potential remedial measures might impose on registries, shipowners, and countries, including impacts on legitimate stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicited stakeholder perspectives and targeted sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission welcomes comments from all members of the public but is particularly interested in input from shippers, carriers, governments, nongovernmental organizations, international standards-setting organizations (e.g., IMO, ITF), and countries with large ship registries or evidence of burdens and risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor submissions to provide sector-specific evidence, policy proposals, or operational data; international standards bodies are encouraged to submit technical or definitional clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence regarding definitions and classification of terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the lack of standardized definitions for terms like 'flag of convenience', 'open registry', 'fraudulent registry', and 'shadow/dark fleet' and how inconsistent definitions affect identification and regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide proposed definitions, taxonomy, or criteria for classification and examples showing how differing definitions lead to inconsistent policy outcomes or enforcement gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission investigatory authority and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that the General Counsel (under 46 U.S.C. 46104 and 46 CFR 502.284) may compel production of information/witnesses and that the Commission may request additional comments or gather more information under applicable statutes and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting data or materials that could be responsive to compelled production, note provenance and availability; anticipate potential follow-up requests for documents or testimony.
